title.narrative: ACF/NRC Food and nutrition security Cabo Delgado
ACF/NRC Livelihoods and food security Cabo Delgado

description.narrative: Insatsen uppgår till en summa av 65 000 000 SEK, med en aktivietsperiod som sträcker sig över tre år. Projektet kommer att inkludera aktiviteter för att återskapa människors försörjningsmöjligheter och öka den socio-ekonomiska motståndskraften, förbättra befolkningens tryggade livsmedelsförsörjning och nutrition och verka för förbättrad lokal kapacitet att reducera och hantera naturkatastrofrelaterade risker.

The contribution proposed will span over three years and 65 000 000 SEK, and will include work to recover people's lost livelihood opportunities and increase socio-economic resilience, improve food security and nutrition and seek to increase local capacities to reduce and manage risks associated with natural hazards.

The overall objective of the programme is to contribute to the creation of appropriate conditions to improve the lives of the rural population living in areas affected by conflict in the province of Cabo Delgado.
Nine communities, in which both IDPs and host populations are present, and in which long-term nexus programming is relevant and feasible, will be selected at the beginning of the intervention.
The programme will prioritise interventions within the food security and livelihoods sector, including activities focusing on water sanitation and hygiene, protection, and health (mainly nutrition). There will also be a disaster risk reduction component to the project for the improved management and reduction of disaster risks.
The specific goals are described below:
- Meet basic food security and livelihood needs of the most vulnerable communities and individuals and improve access to basic services and protection.
- Improve socio-economic resilience and improve food and nutrition security. Support the recovery of the production system, with good agronomic practices, and increase the diversification of livelihoods through providing access to alternative income sources.
- Support the recovery of critical services for the affected host communities and IDPs (markets, health centers, water and sanitation)
- Reduce disaster impact by strengthening local capacities in managing and mitigating disaster risks.
The project aims to reach 20 725 unique beneficiaries, where 15 508 are host community members (including returnees) and 5 217 are IDPs.
